item.title: Why Chiefs are reportedly trading two picks for Colts WR Josh Downs
item.description: Why Chiefs are reportedly trading two picks for Colts WR Josh Downs originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Kansas City Chiefs came into NFL trade deadline day with one very simple goal: acquire a wide receiver to help the offense. While Keenan Allen was dealt to the San Francisco 49ers , there was a different wide receiver from the Indianapolis Colts that they've had their eye on. Finally, with under half an hour to go, they made their move. According to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer , the Chiefs are making a move for Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs. In exchange for a pair of picks, the Chiefs are getting a new WR for Patrick Mahomes. Why Chiefs are trading for Josh Downs from Colts "Trade! The Chiefs are acquiring WR Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Colts for a 2027 fourth-round and fifth-round picks, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports," Pelissero reports. Downs is a rental wide receiver for the Chiefs who instantly provides another solid weapon in the passing game for this offense. He'll join Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy in Kansas City, with running back Kenneth Walker III and tight end Travis Kelce making up a strong offensive supporting cast for Mahomes. The Chiefs are making this trade thanks in large part to Tyquan Thornton's season-ending injury. Add in that Worthy is banged up and has been underwhelming, and a WR addition was a must-have for this team. MORE : Harrison Butker keeps missing field goals and Chiefs fans have had enough A fourth-rounder and a fifth-rounder are a lot to give up for Downs for half a season and a seventh-round pick, but considering their major WR need and the other available options, this is a reasonable move for the Chiefs. Kansas City desperately needed WR help, and Downs might be the best WR traded in the middle of the 2026 season. Marvin Harrison Jr. went for a second-round pick and hasn't been great for the Houston Texans . The Chiefs, meanwhile, take a chance on Downs, who was having a down season with the Colts and their struggling offense. This move shouldn't come as a surprise to anyone, as the Chiefs were strongly implied as the favorites, and now, they're reportedly adding him in a huge move at the trade deadline. item.title: Vikings’ Kirk Cousins trade reunion is a go as Raiders turn to Fernando Mendoza
item.description: David Brytus-Imagn Images Vikings’ Kirk Cousins trade reunion is a go as Raiders turn to Fernando Mendoza appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Minnesota Vikings were desperate to make a trade for a quarterback before the deadline after Monday night’s tough loss to the Buffalo Bills at home. Later in the day on Tuesday, they did just that , reuniting with a familiar face in the process. “Blockbuster! The Raiders are trading four-time Pro Bowl QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings for their 2027 third-round pick,” reported NFL insider Tom Pelissero of The Ringer on X, formerly Twitter. The move reunites the Vikings with Cousins after he spent multiple seasons there with head coach Kevin O’Connell, finding considerable success in the process. Minnesota’s defense has been elite this year but its offense has stumbled, with neither Kyler Murray nor Carson Wentz finding consistent success under center, making it clear that the team had to make a change before the deadline. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Meanwhile, this move now officially hands the keys to number one overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza in Las Vegas. Mendoza has yet to make a start at the NFL level, but that will now change after he spent half of his rookie season learning behind Cousins. Cousins got off to a hot start to the year in Las Vegas, and although he has cooled off a bit in recent weeks, he is still a competent veteran quarterback who should provide an upgrade for the Vikings immediately at the position. In any case, the Vikings will next hit the field on Sunday vs the Green Bay Packers, while Mendoza looks slated to make his first NFL start the same day vs the Seattle Seahawks. item.title: Broncos trade for Chargers LB Daiyan Henley
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 18: Daiyan Henley #0 of the Los Angeles Chargers stands on the field during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to ESPN’s lead league insider, the Denver Broncos have traded for Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley. The Broncos will be sending a 2027 4th-round pick and a 2028 5th-round pick to the Chargers for Henley. Trade: Chargers are sending LB Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos for a 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick, per sources. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 10, 2026 Henley is a 6-0, 225-pound linebacker who was a third-round pick by the Los Angeles Chargers in the 2023 NFL Draft. Throughout his career, Henley has appeared in 56 games and totaled 317 tackles, 5 sacks, 1 forced fumble, 4 interceptions, and 15 pass deflections during his time with the Chargers. This season, Henley has appeared in 8 games and totaled 51 tackles, 0.5 sacks, 1 forced fumble, 1 interception (which happened this past Sunday), and 2 pass deflections. Henley turns 27 years old here in a few days and is in the final year of his rookie deal, but figures to have a role in the Broncos’ defense moving forward. In the short term, Henley will play behind veteran starters Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad , according to reports, but he is a talented linebacker who can cover and blitz, so he should earn some playing time rather quickly. The Broncos are sending a 2027 4th-round pick to the Chargers, but are expected to get a 4th-round compensation pick due to John Franklin-Myers signing with the Titans in free agency this offseason. I really like this pick. Henley is a talented player who gives the Broncos something they really need. An athletic linebacker with sideline-to-sideline speed that can cover and cover well. He’s an excellent coverage linebacker and can cover tight ends and running backs in the pass game, which has been a multi-year issue for the Broncos. Justin Strnad has graded out as one of the better coverage linebackers in the NFL, while Alex Singleton has struggled in that area. Singleton has been solid in the run game, but if he were to come off the field on third downs for Henley, I think that would improve the Broncos’ third-down defense. However, we have to see how the Broncos handle this moving forward, but obviously they have a vision for him since they traded for him. With Henley in the final year of his deal, and the fact that the Broncos traded a 4th-round pick for him, he seems like a player the team views as part of their future. Time will tell there, but it seems like a move for a player they plan on having beyond this season.

item.title: Shawn Horcoff Addresses the Dylan Larkin Trade Standoff
item.description: Detroit Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff met with reporters at the NHL general managers’ meetings in Toronto on Tuesday, and nothing he said moved either of the two situations hanging over his roster. Asked about the Dylan Larkin trade standoff and Simon Edvinsson’s unsigned contract, Horcoff said it was “status quo” with both players. Oct 26, 2026; Edmonton, Alberta, CAN; Edmonton Oilers defensemen Ryan Shea (6) looks to clear the puck in front of Detroit Red Wings forward Dylan Larkin (71) during the second period at Rogers Place. Mandatory Credit: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Horcoff declined to comment on Dylan Larkin’s trade list The one detail that would tell everyone how close this is to ending stayed off the table. Nicholas J. Cotsonika of NHL.com reported that “Horcoff declined to comment on whether Larkin has altered the list of teams to which he would agree to be traded.” Horcoff did describe what a resolution has to look like from Detroit’s side. “Ideally, we get something that works for both sides, right?” he said . “But it has to be something that helps this team.” Larkin still has only 10 teams on his list The Red Wings would like Larkin to open up his approved list, and so far it has not changed. TSN’s Pierre LeBrun reported that Detroit has exhausted its options with the current 10 teams and would like to go deeper in talks with six to eight clubs outside them, while Larkin’s camp believes the list is already long enough. As long as it stays at 10, the market Detroit can actually work is small. Per LeBrun, the 10 teams are the New Jersey Devils, the Colorado Avalanche, the Vegas Golden Knights, the Dallas Stars, the Minnesota Wild, the Washington Capitals, the Utah Mammoth, the Carolina Hurricanes, the Tampa Bay Lightning and the Florida Panthers. Larkin is suspended without pay for now, which means Horcoff and the Red Wings can take their time with a trade. The 30-year-old center has played in 10 games this season for the Red Wings. Larkin scored two goals and recorded four assists with a plus-3 rating, according to ESPN . Horcoff still wants to sign Simon Edvinsson The other half of the status quo carries a hard date. Edvinsson, 23, is an unsigned restricted free agent working out in Nashville, and Cotsonika reported that the defenseman must sign by Dec. 1 to be eligible to play this season. Horcoff has said he has no interest in trading Edvinsson, and on Tuesday he did not close the door on listening. “I’d still like to sign Simon, but I think when it’s someone like that and the situation that we’re in, you can’t help but take calls,” Horcoff said. He added that his job is to do what is in the best interest of the Red Wings, and that he will take those calls and hear what other teams have to say.

item.title: Kyle Busch’s Hauler Drives Away For The Final Time At Homestead
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The No. 8 hauler left Homestead-Miami Speedway on Sunday night for the very last time, marking a somber end to the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series season. After the championship race concluded, the 1.5-mile track was exited by this massive truck, which bore the signature of the late Kyle Busch, as it drove through the tunnel. Fans watched a video by Motorsport showing the team loading up the equipment out of deep respect for the driver who won 234 races across the top three series before his sudden death in May. Austin Hill took over the ride for Richard Childress Racing, piloting the No. 33 Chevrolet to a 15th-place finish in the finale. The team changed the car number from 8 to 33 to honor Busch, yet they kept the old hauler on site until this final departure. In 2027, Hill is scheduled to return full-time to the No. 33, shouldering a season marked by both a championship and a tragedy. His best effort this year came at Talladega with a 14th-place result, but Sunday was about saying goodbye. A Season of Highs and Lows The 2026 season will forever be remembered for two Kyles: Kyle Larson’s dominant playoff surge and Kyle Busch’s shocking death. Larson clinched his third Cup Series title during the opening stage of the finale, finishing 12th at Homestead-Miami Speedway to cap a 49-point victory over Christopher Bell. Even though Larson became the 11th driver in history to win three titles, he refused to look back at his achievements while the sport mourned. “I just feel like when you’re in it and you’re competing, it’s just so hard to reflect in the moment,” Larson said, according to a report . He added that he still has more to accomplish and plans to keep looking out the windshield rather than stopping to admire the rearview mirror. The championship celebration at the annual awards banquet on Tuesday will likely name Busch the most popular driver, honoring a man who died after severe pneumonia progressed into sepsis. Final Tributes At The Track NASCAR leadership made sure the memory of “Rowdy” stayed front and center during the final race. Every fan in the grandstands received a No. 8 Busch flag, and a memorial graphic dedicated to him was painted directly on the frontstretch. The NBC TV booth observed a silent Lap 8 in his honor, with many attendees holding up eight fingers to pay tribute to the two-time champion. “It’s tough to not talk about Kyle when you’re back in Miami,” NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell said. He described Busch as an extraordinary competitor who won the championship at this very track and left a forever mark on the sport. O’Donnell admitted that celebrating a championship feels different without him, noting that the community still misses him deeply. Busch won both of his Cup titles in 2015 and 2019 at Homestead, making his final farewell at this venue even more poignant.

item.title: Colts reportedly trading WR Josh Downs to Chiefs after receiver requested a trade
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - Josh Downs of the Indianapolis Colts lines up against the Tennessee Titans. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Justin Casterline via Getty Images Josh Downs is the latest player to leave Indianapolis after the Colts reportedly dealt the wide receiver to the Kansas City Chiefs, according to Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport . Per Tom Pelissero , the Chiefs, who are also acquiring a 2027 seventh-round draft pick, are sending a fourth- and fifth-round pick in 2027 back to Indianapolis. The addition of the two picks will give the Colts a total of 13 in the 2027 draft. They still do not have a first-round selection after trading it to the New York Jets last season in the Sauce Gardner deal. Downs posted on social media after reports of the trade broke and was very relieved the matter was finally over. pic.twitter.com/SWGjirDe9N — JD (@JoshDowns) November 10, 2026 The 25-year-old Downs, who is set to become a free agent in the offseason, requested a trade away. His move follows the exits of guard Quenton Nelson , defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and wide receiver Keenan Allen , who have been shipped out with the team off to a 2-7 start. Downs was the Colts' third-round pick in the 2023 draft out of North Carolina. He recorded 1,574 receiving yards on 140 catches and seven touchdowns over his first two seasons. This season, with Alec Pierce out due to injury, Downs led the Colts with 354 receiving yards and 57 targets. This story will be updated

item.title: 😳 384 logos on one shirt? Club plans craziest stunt ever
item.description: 😳 384 logos on one shirt? Club plans craziest stunt ever Why have one big main sponsor when you can have 384 (!)? Yes, you read that right: Brazilian club São Joseense, from the state of Paraná, is flipping the script for the 2027 season. Instead of signing a single mega-deal, the club is turning its new shirt into a colorful mosaic for the local community, with a whopping 384 advertising spaces. Each advertising space measures a compact 3.5 by 3.5 centimeters. Depending on whether the logo takes pride of place on the chest or ends up nearer the hem, interested sponsors will pay between 2,000 and 15,000 reais (roughly €300 to €2,500). But what is the club hoping to achieve? According to a press release, the aim is to give small businesses the chance to buy advertising space on the club's shirt. "Being a main sponsor costs a lot of money, which severely limits who can get involved. Our shirt project now gives microbusiness owners and sports enthusiasts an affordable way in," explained Eduardo Grassi. The club's managing director also emphasized: "We want business owners and fans to feel part of this sporting journey—in a city that lives and breathes football but has until now lacked a team of its own to identify with. This is another step toward making São Joseense more prominent and better equipped for a year full of sporting challenges awaiting us in 2027." Among other things, the club will make its debut in the prestigious Brazilian cup competition, the Copa do Brasil. For the mini-sponsors, that means exposure and TV airtime that microbusinesses can usually only dream of. Once the design is finalized, the shirts may well look like a giant QR code from a distance. But in the stands and among local businesses, the initiative is probably already creating exactly what every club hopes for: the feeling of being out on the pitch together. 📸 Instagram São Joseense This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.description: We’ve reached NFL and therefore Seattle Seahawks trade deadline week, which often promises to have some interesting deals and rarely actually materializes. Minor or mid-level deals have happened more recently on deadline day itself, so it’s not like we live in a “nothing happens” world. There have admittedly been prominent in-season trades already this year, including the Quenton Nelson and Jeffery Simmons trades just a couple of weeks ago, as well as Joey Porter Jr going to the Dallas Cowboys, and Marvin Harrison Jr heading for the Houston Texans. For the second year in a row, the trade deadline is during Week 10. The Seattle Seahawks are usually active during the deadline, and this year they’ve pulled off one major trade. Will John Schneider cook up another midseason masterclass like he did for Leonard Williams, Quandre Diggs, Carlos Dunlap, and other names from previous deadline deals? Follow Field Gulls’ trade tracker coverage throughout Monday and Tuesday, and we’ll see what the Seahawks will do as they look to get back on track after a sputtering 5-4 start. Have the Seattle Seahawks made any trades during the regular season? Yes. They acquired longtime Indianapolis Colts guard Quenton Nelson for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. Who could the Seahawks potentially put on the trade block? No one immediately springs to mind. The likes of Dante Fowler Jr have rarely played this year but likely wouldn’t fetch much on the trade market. Emanuel Wilson being an unofficial healthy scratch is worth monitoring, although similarly he’s not much of a valuable trade piece, and Seattle may not want to risk moving any capable RB given the injury concerns on the depth chart. Which positions would the Seahawks potentially be most interested in? Edge rusher and wide receiver might be two positions of need for Seattle. item.title: Santi Aldama Fixes Dallas Offense After Brutal Losses
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The Dallas Mavericks finally found their rhythm on Sunday night, crushing the Brooklyn Nets by a staggering 37-point margin. This 130-93 victory marks the team’s largest winning streak of the season so far. Following a slump marked by consecutive defeats against the Sacramento Kings and San Antonio Spurs, the victory arrives. Per The Smoking Cuban , this sharp turnaround coincides directly with the return of Santi Aldama to the starting lineup. Aldama is filling a roster spot and solving specific problems that plagued the offense all year. The team struggled mightily in their last game against Utah, shooting just 41.9 percent from the field and a poor 28.1 percent from three-point range. However, the energy shifted instantly when Aldama got back on the court. According to The Smoking Cuban , the Mavericks have improved considerably in offensive rebounding and second-chance points specifically because of his presence. The Second-Chance Fix For a long time, Dallas could not secure loose balls near the rim. Throughout the whole league last year, the squad placed 22nd for offensive rebounding and 24th for second-chance points. One year prior, the Mavericks ranked among the NBA’s poorest scoring teams after a missed shot. That stat line has flipped in a hurry. Against the Utah Jazz, Dallas outrebounded the opponent 21-8 on the offensive glass. This dominance led to a massive 21-5 advantage in second-chance points. Aldama alone grabbed nine rebounds in that game, with four of them coming on the offensive end. Versatility Creates Mismatches The big man’s size alone gives Dallas a bonus that other teams cannot match. He is not pigeonholed into playing only center or power forward, which changes how the offense flows. His shooting skill enables Aldama to occupy the three position, He played even when paired with Morez Johnson Jr. in lineups and Daniel Gafford. His perimeter game was on full display against Brooklyn, where he scored 12 points. He shot 5-of-7 from the floor and hit 2-of-4 from three-point range. Aldama scored in a variety of ways, including a basket off a dribble drive that showed his unique skill set. A New Offensive Identity The length and versatility Aldama brings have already stood out in these recent wins. The 7-foot big man helps the team handle defensive pressure and creates easy looks for teammates. His ability to stretch the floor opens up driving lanes for guards who were previously clogged. The improvement in both rebounding and scoring options suggests the team is only getting better. Per The Smoking Cuban, Aldama is a key reason the Mavericks are now two games above .500.

item.title: Video catches USC announcer's take on targeting call
item.description: He said what? That’s what many were asking regarding longtime USC football radio play-by-play announcer Pete Arbogast’s reaction to Oregon quarterback Dante Moore being knocked out of Saturday’s 41-27 Ducks’ victory at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. The play occurred in the second quarter when Moore scrambled and slid. USC linebacker Desman Stephens II then put his shoulder into Moore’s head, knocking him backward into the turf. Moore lay on the field for several minutes before being taken off on a cart and loaded into an ambulance. Stephens celebrated the hit even after being flagged, leading to a skirmish with several Oregon players. Meanwhile, up in the radio booth, Arbogast said the play did not appear to be targeting and claimed Moore didn’t slide feet-first. Arbogast went on to claim that Stephens went in helmet first and ran into Moore who “ducked into that hit.” “I saw him dive forward,” Arbogast claimed. Radio analyst Shaun Cody, who played defensive line at USC (2001-2004) and spent eight seasons in the NFL (Detroit and Houston), clearly disagreed. “He’s laying feet first,” Cody responded. But Arbogast countered, “Well, he is now because they spun him around.” Cody disagreed again, and Arbogast said he wanted to see the replay, which clearly showed Moore sliding feet-first and Stephens going in head-first, with his right shoulder striking Moore in the head. “Yeah, not a feet-first slide, it’s more of a knee slide,” Arbogast claimed while watching the replay. While it’s one thing not to see clearly a live play from high up in a radio booth, it’s another to watch the replay and claim to see something that didn’t exist. Footage from the USC radio team in the Oregon game 😂😂😂 i can’t believe this is real pic.twitter.com/82HYans8Y9 — Adam Breneman (@AdamBreneman81) September 29, 2026 Cody immediately smirked at Arbogast’s viewpoint; then Arbogast added, “It didn’t look like targeting on the replay to us.” In response, Cody looked directly into the camera, eyes wide, and nodded, clearly disagreeing with Arbogast’s assessment. Homerism? Maybe. Potential advertising fodder for local optometrists to encourage thousands to update their eyeglass prescriptions? Absolutely. Oregon backup quarterback Dylan Raiola replaced Moore and passed for 289 yards and two touchdowns in the win. Moore was later diagnosed with a concussion; he has entered concussion protocol and will be out indefinitely . Moore released a statement saying he would soon return. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. item.content:encoded: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. That’s how basketball works. “That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be,” Morant said. The 36-year-old Holiday, who would be a more natural complement next to Lillard or Morant than they are to each other, made his own case for why the point guard rotation makes sense. “It’s about being a complete basketball player for myself,” he said, “and I think we have a lot of guys like that.” There is a long history of teams talking themselves into superstar additions that make little sense. The Los Angeles Lakers once made a conscious decision to acquire Russell Westbrook and pair him with LeBron James. Nobody made them do that! The talent and star power of a Lillard-Morant backcourt is undeniable. Still, I remain unconvinced that Cronin, with a very hands-on new owner in his ear, made the deal with winning basketball games at the front of mind. Although, admittedly, Cronin’s biggest wins as a GM have been in the trade market. The haul of assets he collected for Lillard, only to get him back two years later, will go down as an all-time great swindle. So, too, will the oft-questioned Avdija trade a year later. Maybe he sees something in a Lillard-Morant pairing that many of us can’t. Morant could return to the All-Star form he had achieved before injuries and off-court issues derailed his ascent . And if he does, the Blazers can either trade him for pieces that fit better or clear out the logjam and build around him. But to sell the current roster as a basketball strategy doesn’t quite pass the smell test. Neither Lillard nor Morant has achieved stardom due to his defensive acumen. Each player needs the ball in his hands to thrive. If the duo is on the floor together, Avdija is no longer the secondary playmaker, he becomes tertiary. So, you are left to wonder whether the Blazers sold themselves on Morant because of how he can help the current collection of talent or if they simply saw the opportunity to land a 27-year-old All-NBA talent for cheap, regardless of what it meant for the existing roster construction. And if you’re being honest, you probably don’t need to wonder which of the two it is. “We were very focused and we’ll continue to be on … adding to our talent base as much as we can,” Cronin said. That thinking right there may tell you just how far ahead of everyone else the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder are in the Western Conference. They are positioned to dominate for the next half-decade, if not longer. The only chance any other team has of disrupting that is taking bold risks. But I thought the goal was to go all in on the twilight years of Lillard’s career? “Dame literally just wants to win,” said first-year head coach Micah Nori, whose charge is to sort out arguably the most talented glut of point guard talent in NBA history. “I think that’s the only thing left he really has to (do). He’s already proven he’s a winner, but at the highest level.” Does adding Morant move Lillard closer to a title? Or simply give Portland a potential off-ramp if Lillard is no longer the same player after tearing his Achilles tendon? Morant was without question a low-risk, high-reward addition. He came at the reasonable price of Jerami Grant and Kris Murray. If it becomes clear that Morant is one point guard too many, or that he’s just not the player he once was, some will argue that it didn’t cost the Blazers much to try. However, there is an opportunity cost to messing with Lillard’s swan song. If you don’t get it right, you risk wasting the gift of his voluntary return last summer . And, not for nothing, Lillard has the option to become a free agent again after this season. The franchise icon certainly hasn’t said anything that would suggest he is unhappy about Morant’s presence, although he stopped short on Monday of a full-throated endorsement. He said he knew about the trade before it went through. When I asked if he thought it was a good idea right away or if he needed time to get on board with the plan, Lillard said, “My position on it was, I’m prepared for whatever.” It’s good that he’s already thinking about other positions. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Parrott in running for hat-trick at FAI awards
item.description: Parrott is nominated for player of the year, young player of the year and goal of the year [Getty Images] Troy Parrott has been shortlisted in three categories for the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) International Awards. The 24-year-old Real Betis striker is in the running for player of the year and young player of the year, while he has two nominations for goal of the year. Parrott helped propel the Republic of Ireland into the World Cup playoffs, scoring both goals in the victory over Portugal in Dublin before netting a hat-trick in the must-win away game against Hungary, while also finding the net from the spot in the play-off defeat by Czech Republic. The Dubliner is a first-time nominee in the player of the year category, joined by Dara O'Shea who also makes the list for the first time, while goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher makes the shortlist for the second year. James Abankwah and Evan Ferguson - who won in 2022 and 2023 - join Parrott on the young player of the year shortlist. Parrott's second goal and last-gasp winner away to Hungary are in consideration for goal of the year along with Katie McCabe's stunning stike in the 3-2 away win against Poland in a World Cup qualifier. The women's national team captain is nominated for women's senior player of the year for a sixth time and the 2021 winner is joined by first-time nominees Emily Murphy and Marissa Sheva. Women's young player of the year will be contested between 2024 winner Jessie Stapleton, three-time nominee Abbie Larkin and Emily Murphy who is included for the first time. Jacob Devaney, Mason Melia and Jamie Mullins are nominated for the men's under-21 award. The performances taken into account for all categories are from June 2025 to May 2026

item.title: Mariners Are Most Obvious Team for Red Sox to Make Blockbuster Trade With
item.description: Mariners Are Most Obvious Team for Red Sox to Make Blockbuster Trade With originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the Boston Red Sox expected to have some needs on the mound, and Sonny Gray expected to depart in free agency, the front office has a few ways to approach this winter. There are a couple of decent starting pitchers out there, but outside of Tarik Skubal, there isn't exactly a lights-out pitcher on this free agency market. There are a couple of intriguing names on the potential trade market, however, with the Seattle Mariners having two of them. It would be questionable for the Mariners to move on from George Kirby or Emerson Hancock, but Seattle has other needs in the offense and could be willing to trade some of those guys for the right package. Whether it would be Seattle getting prospects back or big league talent is one thing, but either way, the Red Sox could be of interest to both of those teams. “The Red Sox built their team on pitching and defense, and they shouldn't go away from that plan in 2027 just because they need to upgrade the offense. The Seattle Mariners have multiple starting pitchers with at least two years of team control that they are willing to listen on. Acquiring one to add to Garrett Crochet, Payton Tolle, and Ranger Suarez would be one of the best rotations in baseball. “The Mariners reportedly want to use one of their pitchers to find an impact bat for their lineup. Breslow could kill two birds with one stone by using one of the outfielders to give them just that. The Red Sox can't go into 2027 with the amount of uncertainty in the bottom two of the rotation they currently have, and getting one of the Mariners' starters would be an excellent long-term fix to that situation,” Brian Burrows wrote . As Burrows noted, the Mariners looking for an offensive player who can come in and help immediately would give the Red Sox multiple options to move on from. Even if they wanted to go the prospect route, there are a few prospects in the Red Sox system who can help out Seattle in the short and long term. For Boston, the bigger thing here would be getting one of these two guys who have elite stuff. Kirby is coming off a season in which he struggled, posting a 4.33 ERA. However, if he can get back to his 2023 and 2024 form, there's reason to believe he can be an elite arm in this Red Sox rotation, especially since he's still just 28. item.title: LIV Golf Shuts Down: The End Of A Five-Year Experiment
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images LIV Golf officially closed up shop on November 5, marking the end of a five-year experiment funded by Saudi Arabia. The league launched with big promises and huge checks, but it could not sustain itself without its primary financial backer. This sudden halt leaves players scrambling for their next moves while the PGA Tour watches from the sidelines. ESPN staff writer Paolo Uggetti shared the details on why the league shut down, noting that the financial support from the Public Investment Fund has dried up. Saudi Arabia’s global sports influence shift was contextualized by Sarath Ganji, who founded the Autocracy and Global Sports Initiative, during this era. The money that once flowed freely to sign top talent is no longer available, forcing an orderly winding-down process. A Failed Vision and a New Reality The dream of a new era for professional golf died quickly once the funding stopped. Phil Mickelson proclaimed LIV would be a game changer that brought the PGA Tour to its knees, but that never happened. It was never destined to become the “force for change and good,” that Bryson DeChambeau once mocked so laughably. According to Lee News Central , LIV amounted to nothing beyond a cash grab. Because it was always amoral at its core and utterly devoid of principles, failure was inevitable like so many other things. From the beginning, Rory McIlroy, who became golf’s conscience through his fierce opposition to LIV, anticipated the conclusion. “I think that there is going to be a bit of a reset here, just for things to be a little bit more sustainable,” McIlroy said on Wednesday, November 4, when it became clear LIV was circling the drain. Players Pivot to New Deals With the league gone, players are already looking for new ways to make money. While he had previously collaborated with the brand on headcovers, this new deal expands their relationship to feature his own dedicated clothing collection. DeChambeau shared seven photographs announcing the news on social media alongside an enthusiastic message for his followers. “I’m excited for this one,” he wrote. “Headcovers were just the start… now I’m expanding my partnership with @swaggolfco into apparel!” The new collection drops November 19 online and in stores at Dick’s Sporting Goods and Golf Galaxy. Despite the league ending, DeChambeau insisted he had no regrets about joining in the summer of 2022. “I’m not going to rewrite the last four years. I made a decision I believed in, and I’m grateful for what came with it,” he wrote. Some might argue the lack of a financial war is bad for players, but McIlroy disagrees. “There’s not as much of an arms race as there was maybe a couple of years ago, and some players will argue that that’s not good for players. I think that’s very short-term thinking,” McIlroy said. “If you want sustainable tours, and we want these tours around in 50 years’ time, there has to be sustainable business practices in place to make sure they are.”

Colts trade Josh Downs to Chiefs And we have another Colts trade. Indianapolis is trading wide receiver Josh Downs to the Kansas City Chiefs, giving Patrick Mahomes another target in the passing game. Here are the full terms of the deal: Chiefs receive: WR Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick Colts receive: A 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick Chargers trade Daiyan Henley to Broncos The Broncos are adding on defense, acquiring linebacker Daiyan Henley from the Los Angeles Chargers in the rare trade between division rivals. After a poor showing on “Monday Night Football,” the Minnesota Vikings are trading for Kirk Cousins. The move brings Cousins back to Minnesota, reuniting him with Kevin O’Connell. It also paves the way for the start of the Fernando Mendoza era in Las Vegas. Here are the full terms of the deal: Vikings receive: Kirk Cousins Raiders receive: A 2027 third-round pick. The Tennessee Titans, having already traded Jeffery Simmons to the Bears, are sending safety Amani Hooker to the Buffalo Bills. It was not a good week on the field for Ole Miss Football . Ole Miss lost to Georgia in embarrassing fashion, falling 42-7 . The loss dropped Ole Miss to 6-3 on the season, as they tumbled to 19th in the AP Poll. While Ole Miss took the loss on the field, they got a win on the college football recruiting trail on Tuesday, per Hayes Fawcett of Rivals. “Class of 2029 WR Matthew Fletcher has Committed to Ole Miss, he tells me for Rivals. The 6’3 200 WR is the No. 1 WR in Mississippi in the 2029 Rivals300. ‘This is where I see my future #HottyToddy'” Fawcett posted on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Fletcher is the top player for the class of 2029 out of Mississippi. He is currently ranked as a three-star recruit. Fletcher also spoke about why he chose Ole Miss, per Zach Berry of On3. “I love the school. They have been top of my list after I first visited for a practice,” Fletcher said. “Ole Miss is home to be honest.” Fletcher, who is currently a high school sophomore, chose the Rebels over offers from Florida, Florida State, LSU, and Mississippi State. “Ole Miss just felt like home to me from the beginning. The coaching staff has been great throughout this whole process and has made me feel like a priority,” Fletcher said. “I love the environment the coaches are building and the direction the program is headed. I feel like Ole Miss is the best place for me to develop not only as a football player, but as a person. After talking with my family and thinking everything through, I felt like this was where I wanted my future to be. Still looking at other schools, too, but this is where I see myself right now.” Fletcher is the second member of the class of 2029 to sign with the Rebels, joining Athlete Jordan Husband. item.title: NFL reporter says emoji sums up Eagles' reaction to Bengals trade nix
item.description: ESPN/NFL Network reporter Mike Garafolo tweeted that the Philadelphia Eagles were not happy that a trade with the Cincinnati Bengals involving defensive end Arnold Ebiketie appears to have fallen through because of an issue with compensatory picks. "Vibes in the Eagles' building right now after this one fell through: 🤬," Garafolo tweeted . ESPN NFL analyst Field Yates credited Over the Cap contributor Nick Korte, considered an expert on compensatory picks rules, with helping the Bengals for the second time in three years, with tweets earlier that followed Ian Rapoport's announcement of the reported trade, which Rapoport later reported wasn't finalized . Sports agent Drew Rosenhaus appeared on ESPN's "Pat McAfee Show" and suggested that the trade may have fizzled because Ebiketie didn't want to play for the Bengals. item.title: NFL trade deadline 2026: Denver Broncos latest news and rumors
item.description: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks at the scoreboard during the second quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2 p.m. MT, and our Denver Broncos could be an active team prior to the deadline. They have been widely connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor in the days leading up to the deadline , but according to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the team could explore adding a weapon or two to their offense. He mentions running back, tight end, and wide receiver as the positions that they could add. With Harvey injury and Badie also on IR and injuries across the offense, would expect Broncos to explore adding a weapon or two before trade deadline (RB, TE, WR). https://t.co/TSad3tJ2d3 — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) October 31, 2026 Looking at the Broncos’ needs heading into the deadline, the most glaring one is running back. Now, the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman helps, but the Broncos still need more from the position. RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie are on the injured reserve, and veteran JK Dobbins has been struggling all season. So, adding another back to pair with Coleman would make sense. The question is, will they go big and add a Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall? Or make a smaller move for someone like Tony Pollard or someone else? Klis mentions wide receiver, and while it may not be the most pressing need right now, it could be in a few months. Jaylen Waddle has not performed as expected thus far; Courtland Sutton will be 32 next season and has a large cap hit(Also restructured his deal and could be off the team next season); Pat Bryant has been very good, but has been on the IR; Marvin Mims is a pending free agent, while Troy Franklin is buried on the depth chart. Could the Broncos be looking to add a wide receiver who could contribute to this team this season and moving forward? This doesn’t seem as likely, but I wouldn’t rule it out if the right deal comes their way. As for tight end, I don’t know. The only name that could move the needle and that might be available is Dallas Goedert, but is that even worth it? He would certainly improve that room, but the Broncos really do not utilize their tight ends in the passing game. Evan Engram has had a disappointing year, and blocking specialist Nate Adkins leads the group (and, funny enough, the team) in TD receptions with 3, but he only has 6 total catches thus far. We’ll be tracking all the Broncos news and rumors throughout the weekend and right up to the deadline. It’s supposed to be an active deadline, so we’ll see if our Denver Broncos make any splashes or not in the coming days. Some notable trade Candidates Colts RB Jonathan Taylor Colts WR Josh Downs Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr. Titans RB Tony Pollard Eagles TE Dallas Goedert Chargers EDGE Khalil Mack Cardin

item.description: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images The temptation to rest South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers is growing loud among fans. Many worry his injured ankle could get worse if he plays on Saturday night. Coach Shane Beamer told reporters on Sunday that the team fully expects their star player to take the field. He disclosed the details of the injury and stated his position. Sellers limped to a game-winning touchdown against Texas A&M. Now he faces Arkansas, and the staff have already made a decision. Coach Beamer Confirms Sellers Status Beamer spoke directly about the tests Sellers took on Sunday. The results came back clean, which gives the staff confidence. “We fully expect him to play,” Beamer said, according to a report . He added that the player got some tests done and everything looked good with the results. The quarterback did not practice Sunday evening, and the team does not practice on Mondays. The schedule does not indicate Sellers is out. Beamer expects his Heisman Trophy candidate to be under center against the Razorbacks. “We feel good about his availability this weekend,” Beamer said. The coach noted that the only real issue is pain tolerance. “Right now, it’s nothing that concerns us aside from his pain tolerance and getting some of the swelling down in that ankle,” he explained. Why Sitting Him Is a Bad Move Sellers has already proven his worth with two huge moments this season. He pushed aside two Tennessee defenders for a score and then limped for a 41-yard touchdown against Texas A&M. These are signature moments that Heisman voters remember. The risk of sitting him now outweighs the benefit of rest. Arkansas has struggled terribly throughout almost the entire season, securing only a single SEC victory. It is the total number of wins against Power 4 teams. The Gamecocks cannot afford to lose to a bad team. Provided Sellers is healthy and cleared, he ought to play at Razorbacks Stadium this Saturday night. The talk of a College Football Playoff spot ends with a loss to the Razorbacks. item.description: Arizona Cardinals v Seattle Seahawks Getty Derick Hall is one of the key reasons the Seattle Seahawks are the defending Super Bowl champions. Things haven’t been perfect this season for Seattle as it’s been an up-and-down year. They’re 5-4 and in the thick of the NFC playoff race, but they’ve been forced to deal with key injuries to starters Sam Darnold and Zach Charbonnet. Seattle has been able to weather the storm and they’ve been able to pick up key victories, including handing the Kansas City Chiefs their first loss while also beating the Patriots in the season opener. It’s the reason why he’s partnering with Huggies leading into World Prematurity Day (Nov. 15). “That’s 100% correct,” said Hall of the biggest message from his life story is being of resilience. “And more than anything, it takes a village to raise a child. The main piece for me is my mom. My mom was my advocate. Being a premie baby, you need someone to fight for. You need someone to advocate for you, so that being your mother, your father, your family, and then you have the secondary level of that, which is Huggies, and myself and my foundation. It’s just so huge to have that belief, that resilience, that fight, and know that someone is fighting for you. O “Obviously as a kid, a little infant baby, you can’t realize those things, but as you begin to grow, because these hardships can last for good bit of time in the adolescent years of their lif, you begin to see who’s been there for you and who’s the people who’s been doing the background work. Your parents advocating for yo, so that’s true to us about resilience, fight, toughness, grit, connection and then just having people to fight for you, getting your parents Huggies, and then having an opportunity to do this. Which is so special to me about giving back and having this opportunity myself.” Hall details his partnership with Huggies even further and the message he’s trying to spread through his foundation. “This partnership with Huggies came about obviously partially due to my story and NICU Awareness Month,” said Hall. “That’s really where it all started for me. This partnership, a lot of people know my story. I was a premie, given a 1% chance to live, and Huggies has been doing the the background work for premies for years and years. When I had this opportunity to partner with them, it was a no brainer for me and my foundation, the Derick Foundation, and my family. It’s just so key to have somebody fighting for you, being at bat, being combative for you and your family. It’s such a hardship because being a premie parent isn’t easy. “Going through all these hardships, knowing that there’s someone to show you the love, support, and connection in Huggies, and then the foundation of myself is just so huge,” said Hall. “You have World Premature Day coming up on November 15. So just in that opportunity, spread that light, spread that joy, let families know what Huggies is doing for premie babies in those moments, and let them know that there are people there to support you and help you through those hardships and those hard moments. It’s amazing. it’s something truly special, and I’m just looking forward to continue to grow this partnership and continue to know Huggies at a deeper level, and them obviously know me at a deeper level, so it’s amazing.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Seahawks’ Derick Hall’s Message to Klint Kubiak Before Raiders Game appeared first on HEAVY .

Where the hell is Roy Keane! How dare you leave out Bobby Moore! And Pelé? A list without Pelé? I don’t want to live in a world where there are lists without Pelé. Such is the world these days, though surely a certain amount of respect is due to an exercise that shuns Lionel Messi and Zinedine Zidane but can welcome in Salvatore Sirigu and Mateusz Klich. And true, it might be a challenging read for those (and, let’s be clear, we’re absolutely definitely not referring to ourselves here, no sirree) old enough to have been brought up in an era of 1; 2, 5, 6, 3; 7, 4, 8, 11; 9 (big man), 10 (little man). item.title: From W-M to the No 10, shirt numbers tell a story of football’s tactical evolution
item.description: In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, as well as the attributes a player was supposed to demonstrate Ultimate 1-50: check out our complete list of players Numbers have a fascination. The No 10 is revered almost everywhere, but perhaps most especially in Argentina, where it denotes the playmaker, the enganche , the quasi-mythical figure who links the front and back of the team. Liverpool and Manchester United have reasons to celebrate their No 7. Ajax retired No 14 for Johan Cruyff, Milan their No 3 and No 6 for Paolo Maldini and Franco Baresi respectively and Birmingham their 22 for Jude Bellingham as gestures of respect for their abilities. Other numbers have been retired to mark premature deaths: the No 20 at Liverpool for Diogo Jota, the No 23 at Manchester City for Marc-Vivian Foé, the 21 at Espanyol for Daniel Jarque. But numbers are not just about individuals. In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, and the expectations of particular numbers in particular cultures, as well as the attributes a player in that shirt was supposed to demonstrate, themselves tell a story of tactical evolution. item.title: Football Daily | Manchester United, Aston Villa and the unseriousness of a 4-4 draw
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Precisely 13,266 games have been played since the inception of the Premier League, and 19 of those matches have finished 4-4 (0.1%), a rarity in a division dominated by the mighty 1-0 (17.6%). It was about time we got one, though. The months of August and September, when teams are still fighting to define their top-flight seasons and fitness and motivation tend to be at their peak, have never seen a single 4-4 draw. As motivation decreases the chances of stupid scorelines increase, and that’s where the 4-4 creeps in. There’s a certain on-the-beachness inherent in the score, and it is no coincidence that it has occurred more in the second half of April, as thoughts drift to the close season and the ineffable pointlessness of a lot of late-campaign football becomes unavoidable, than in the entirety of any other month. Students, teachers and visitors at the University of Queensland can view the world’s longest-running experiment. Nearly 100 years ago pitch was placed in a funnel and kept at room temperature. It moves incredibly slowly at a rate of approximately one atom per second (slower than the continental drift), and only nine drips have ever been recorded , though never witnessed. item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Has a footballer ever run a marathon faster than James Milner? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: managers sacked after signing new deals, war victims commemorated on kits and the first club website (part II) Mail us with all of your questions and answers It came as no surprise to the Knowledge that James Milner had spent the early months of his retirement training for – and then running in – the New York City Marathon. Yes, the bleep test-loving former Brighton, Liverpool and Manchester City player recorded an excellent time of 3hr 9min 4sec, an average of 7min 13sec per mile. Not bad for a 40-year-old whose physique is more like that of a wrestler than a whippet. “A few years ago, I feel like I could have definitely done sub-3:00,” he said, lamenting his late-career injuries for hindering him. In 2012 we ran a column listing footballers’ fastest marathon times, with the former Leicester playmaker Muzzy Izzet leading the pack on 3hr 22min 36sec at the 2011 London Marathon. That very respectable time has now been surpassed by the Premier League’s record appearance maker, so we thought we had better take a gulp of our isotonic energy drink and run through a few more tales of football’s marathon men and women. item.description: Inspired by the legendary Milan sides of his youth, the manager gave his side a lift with a tactical victory over Inter Ruben Amorim had waited a lifetime for his first Milan derby. item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. item.title: Folarin Balogun takes a first, tiny step toward moving on from a calamitous summer
item.description: The USMNT striker scored his first goal since the World Cup in a losing effort against Paris FC. Could it lead to something more? Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. item.title: Rampant Salford hint that Beckham’s lofty ambitions are not a pipe dream
item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. Match-winner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
